tool.excerpt: == Campaign == === First round === Sławomir Mentzen of the Confederation alliance was the first candidate to begin an electoral campaign on 31 August 2024, drawing criticism and accusations of illegality from politicians of other parties for its early start. Marshal of the Sejm Szymon Hołownia from the Poland 2050 party declared his candidacy on 13 November. The Civic Coalition (KO) selected its candidate in a presidential primary on 22 November after Minister of Foreign Affairs Radosław Sikorski challenged presumptive nominee, Mayor of Warsaw Rafał Trzaskowski, who was KO's 2020 presidential candidate. Following the KO primary, Institute of National Remembrance chairman Karol Nawrocki was endorsed by the Law and Justice party on 24 November as an officially independent candidate, as he never belonged to any political party. Other groups also ran their own candidates. ... Presidential elections were held in Poland on 18 May 2025. As no candidate received a majority of the vote, a second round was held on 1 June 2025. Incumbent president Andrzej Duda was ineligible for re-election to a third term. The second round was won by conservative Institute of National Remembrance director Karol Nawrocki, with 50.89% of the vote, who was backed by the Law and Justice (PiS) party. Anniversary Marked by Political Attacks Exactly one year ago, Karol Nawrocki took the oath of office before the National Assembly and assumed the office of President of the Republic of Poland.
Government spokesperson Adam Szłapka wrote: “Karol Nawrocki’s record after one year as president is 41 vetoes.

The president has also repeatedly emphasized that he exercises his veto power whenever he believes legislation passed by parliament fails to adequately protect the public interest, the security of Polish citizens, or the standards of sound lawmaking.
First-Year Record The Chancellery of the President states that Karol Nawrocki’s first year in office reflected the commitments he made during the presidential campaign.

The balance of the first twelve months includes 22 legislative initiatives, 255 bills signed into law, and 41 vetoes – figures that, on the anniversary of Karol Nawrocki’s presidency, have become the subject of an intense political dispute.
“Poles would be wealthier and safer today if not for President Nawrocki’s actions over the past year.
Forty-one blocked bills are slowing Poland’s development and making life more difficult for Polish citizens,” he wrote.
They omit the rest of Karol Nawrocki’s first-year record.
Each time Karol Nawrocki refused to sign a bill, he publicly explained the reasons for his decision.

Adam Szłapka, Jan Grabiec and Krzysztof Gawkowski accuse the president of relying too heavily on his veto power, while overlooking the fact that during his first year in office he signed 255 bills into law, submitted 22 legislative initiatives of his own, and provided detailed public explanations for every veto.

While politicians from the right are summarizing the first year of his presidency, representatives of Donald Tusk’s coalition have spent the day posting a series of critical messages about the head of state on social media.
The most frequently repeated accusation concerns the number of presidential vetoes.

According to a summary published by the Chancellery of the President, during his first twelve months in office the head of state signed 255 bills into law, submitted 22 legislative initiatives, and focused his work on strengthening national security, enhancing Poland’s position on the international stage, legislative activity, and exercising the constitutional powers of the presidency.

Every Veto Was Accompanied by an Explanation The presidential veto is one of the constitutional prerogatives of the President of the Republic of Poland and serves as an element of oversight in the legislative process.

In every case, he identified the specific provisions that raised concerns and argued that certain measures required amendments or could have negative consequences for citizens and the functioning of the state.

Its summary lists national security, the development of the president’s own legislative initiatives, international engagement, and the consistent exercise of the constitutional duties of the head of state among his key priorities.

tool.excerpt: Twitter and Research: A Systematic Literature Review Through Text Mining. Researchers have collected Twitter data to study a wide range of topics. This growing body of literature, however, has not yet been reviewed systematically to synthesize Twitter-related papers. The existing literature review papers have been limited by constraints of traditional methods to manually select and analyze samples of topically related papers. The goals of this retrospective study are to identify dominant topics of Twitter-based research, summarize the temporal trend of topics, and interpret the evolution of topics withing the last ten years. This study systematically mines a large number of Twitter-based studies to characterize the relevant literature by an efficient and effective approach. This study collected relevant papers from three databases and applied text mining and trend analysis to detect semantic patterns and explore the yearly development of research themes across a decade. We found 38 topics in more than 18,000 manuscripts published between 2006 and 2019. By quantifying temporal trends, this study found that while 23.7% of topics did not show a significant trend (P = 0.05), 21% of topics had increasing trends and 55.3% of topics had decreasing trends that these hot and cold topics represent three categories: application, methodology, and technology. The contributions of this paper can be utilized in the growing field of Twitter-based research and are beneficial to researchers, educators, and publishers.

tool.excerpt: == Campaign == === First round === Sławomir Mentzen of the Confederation alliance was the first candidate to begin an electoral campaign on 31 August 2024, drawing criticism and accusations of illegality from politicians of other parties for its early start. Marshal of the Sejm Szymon Hołownia from the Poland 2050 party declared his candidacy on 13 November. The Civic Coalition (KO) selected its candidate in a presidential primary on 22 November after Minister of Foreign Affairs Radosław Sikorski challenged presumptive nominee, Mayor of Warsaw Rafał Trzaskowski, who was KO's 2020 presidential candidate. Following the KO primary, Institute of National Remembrance chairman Karol Nawrocki was endorsed by the Law and Justice party on 24 November as an officially independent candidate, as he never belonged to any political party. Other groups also ran their own candidates. ... Presidential elections were held in Poland on 18 May 2025. As no candidate received a majority of the vote, a second round was held on 1 June 2025. Incumbent president Andrzej Duda was ineligible for re-election to a third term. The second round was won by conservative Institute of National Remembrance director Karol Nawrocki, with 50.89% of the vote, who was backed by the Law and Justice (PiS) party. tool.title: 2025 Polish presidential election
tool.excerpt: == Campaign == === First round === Sławomir Mentzen of the Confederation alliance was the first candidate to begin an electoral campaign on 31 August 2024, drawing criticism and accusations of illegality from politicians of other parties for its early start. Marshal of the Sejm Szymon Hołownia from the Poland 2050 party declared his candidacy on 13 November. The Civic Coalition (KO) selected its candidate in a presidential primary on 22 November after Minister of Foreign Affairs Radosław Sikorski challenged presumptive nominee, Mayor of Warsaw Rafał Trzaskowski, who was KO's 2020 presidential candidate. Following the KO primary, Institute of National Remembrance chairman Karol Nawrocki was endorsed by the Law and Justice party on 24 November as an officially independent candidate, as he never belonged to any political party. Signup Top Stories Kashmir Politics Developing Story National Anchor Opinion Editorial Viewpoint Technology Powered by : Advertisment Breaking News Breaking Assam: 12 killed, 25 injured after truck-bus collision in Golaghat ANI 03 Jan 2024 09:03 IST Follow Us At least 12 people were killed and 25 others injured after a bus where they were travelling, collided with a truck in Assam's Golaghat district on Wednesday morning, police said. According to police, the accident took place in the Balijan area near Dergaon in Golaghat district. Rajen Singh, Superintendent of Police of Golaghat district told ANI that, the accident occurred at around 5 am on Wednesday. "The bus carrying a team was going towards Tilinga Mandir from the Kamarbandha area of Golaghat district. The bus collided with a truck in the Balijan area and the truck was coming in the opposite direction from Jorhat's side. 10 bodies were recovered from the site and sent to Dergaon CHC. 27 injured persons were referred to Jorhat Medical College & Hospital where two people succumbed to their injuries," Rajen Singh said. Following the incident, locals rushed to the site and engaged in rescue operations. The SP of Golaghat district said that, so far 12 people died in the accident. "Our investigation is on and we will take action as per law," Rajen Singh said. More details awaited. (ANI) Read More Subscribe to our Newsletter! tool.title: 2026 Gagauz general election
tool.excerpt: General elections took place in Moldova's autonomous region of Gagauzia on 15 November 2026 to elect the region's Governor (Gagauz: Başkan) and the members of Gagauzia's local parliament, the People's Assembly of Gagauzia. In the first round of the gubernatorial election, PSRM's Fiodor Gagauz and independent Alexandr Stoianoglo advanced to the runoff to be held on 29 November 2026, alongside the rest of the People's Assembly seats. == History == On 1 September 2026, the Central Electoral Commission (CEC) of Moldova scheduled general elections for 15 November in the autonomous region of Gagauzia to elect both the region's Governor (Gagauz: Başkan) and the members of the People's Assembly of Gagauzia, the region's local parliament. The move brought to an end a legislative deadlock in the region following the conviction of the previous governor, Evghenia Guțul, who received a seven-year sentence over illegal financing related to the outlawed Șor Party. On 21 September, Grigorii Uzun, a member of the Party of Socialists of the Republic of Moldova (PSRM), announced that he would not run in the election for the post of governor. This was despite him having been considered the PSRM's likeliest candidate, with Uzun being who ran in the 2023 gubernatorial election in the second round against Guțul. His announcement was due to the fact that he did not speak Romanian ("Moldovan", as he called it) at the time, as new provisions had been adopted in the electoral code in August requiring candidates for the post to speak both Gagauz and Romanian. Subsequently, on 24 September, the PSRM announced it would back Fiodor Gagauz, who submitted his registration documents to run as a candidate for governorship on the same day. Gagauz had been a member of Gagauzia's People's Assembly between 2012 and 2014 and had held three consecutive mandates as member of the Parliament of Moldova since 2014. == Analysis == On 10 September, Igor Grosu, the President of the Parliament of Moldova, asserted that the Gagauz general election should take place in a fair and transparent manner and that the authorities would not tolerate attempts to bribe voters or buy their votes or other maneuvers to influ

His announcement was due to the fact that he did not speak Romanian ("Moldovan", as he called it) at the time, as new provisions had been adopted in the electoral code in August requiring candidates for the post to speak both Gagauz and Romanian. tool.excerpt: General elections took place in Moldova's autonomous region of Gagauzia on 15 November 2026 to elect the region's Governor (Gagauz: Başkan) and the members of Gagauzia's local parliament, the People's Assembly of Gagauzia. The move brought to an end a legislative deadlock in the region following the conviction of the previous governor, Evghenia Guțul, who received a seven-year sentence over illegal financing related to the outlawed Șor Party. On 21 September, Grigorii Uzun, a member of the Party of Socialists of the Republic of Moldova (PSRM), announced that he would not run in the election for the post of governor. This was despite him having been considered the PSRM's likeliest candidate, with Uzun being who ran in the 2023 gubernatorial election in the second round against Guțul. His announcement was due to the fact that he did not speak Romanian ("Moldovan", as he called it) at the time, as new provisions had been adopted in the electoral code in August requiring candidates for the post to speak both Gagauz and Romanian. Subsequently, on 24 September, the PSRM announced it would back Fiodor Gagauz, who submitted his registration documents to run as a candidate for governorship on the same day. tool.excerpt: General elections took place in Moldova's autonomous region of Gagauzia on 15 November 2026 to elect the region's Governor (Gagauz: Başkan) and the members of Gagauzia's local parliament, the People's Assembly of Gagauzia. The move brought to an end a legislative deadlock in the region following the conviction of the previous governor, Evghenia Guțul, who received a seven-year sentence over illegal financing related to the outlawed Șor Party. On 21 September, Grigorii Uzun, a member of the Party of Socialists of the Republic of Moldova (PSRM), announced that he would not run in the election for the post of governor. This was despite him having been considered the PSRM's likeliest candidate, with Uzun being who ran in the 2023 gubernatorial election in the second round against Guțul. His announcement was due to the fact that he did not speak Romanian ("Moldovan", as he called it) at the time, as new provisions had been adopted in the electoral code in August requiring candidates for the post to speak both Gagauz and Romanian. Subsequently, on 24 September, the PSRM announced it would back Fiodor Gagauz, who submitted his registration documents to run as a candidate for governorship on the same day. She broke the world record with a throw of 77.44 m in the qualifying round of the 1986 European Athletics Championships in Stuttgart, and became the first British athlete to set a world record in a throwing event. Whitbread went on to win the European title that year, and took the gold medal at the 1987 World Championships. She is also a two-time Olympic medallist, winning bronze at the 1984 Summer Olympics and silver at the 1988 Summer Olympics. sentences: Până acum, și-au mai anunțat intenția de a candida Fiodor Gagauz, fost deputat în Parlament, Alexandr Stoianoglo, fost procuror general și actual deputat al fracțiunii „Alternativa”, precum și fostul deputat Petr Vlah.

Liderul organizației teritoriale a Partidului Socialiștilor a anunțat într-o conferință de presă că a luat această decizie întrucât nu cunoaște „limba moldovenească”, în contextul în care noile prevederi ale Codului Electoral, adoptate în august, obligă candidații să cunoască limbile română și găgăuză.

La o conferință de presă susținută alături de liderul partidului, Igor Dodon, parlamentarul a acuzat majoritatea parlamentară că a modificat intenționat, cu puțin timp înainte de alegeri, Codul electoral, introducând o normă care limitează participarea la scrutin a persoanelor care nu vorbesc limba de stat.
Am luat decizia de a nu-mi depune candidatura la alegerile pentru funcția de bașcan”, a declarat Uzun, care a criticat noile prevederi ale Codului Electoral.
Igor Dodon a mai declarat, că modificarea legislației electorale cu doar două săptămâni înainte de perioada electorală este contrară Constituției și practicilor europene.
Condiția privind cunoașterea limbii trebuia să fie introdusă începând cu următorul ciclu electoral, peste patru ani”, a afirmat Dodon.
Scrutinele se vor desfășura după noile prevederi ale Codului Electoral al Republicii Moldova, întrucât Codul Electoral al autonomiei nu mai este valabil.
În listele electorale din regiune sunt înscriși în jur de 129.000 de alegători.

This act was apparently a reference to the alleged violation of the ballot secrecy in the elections, in particular the issue of thin ballot papers which made it visible from the outside which party a citizen was voting for. It has subsequently been expanded to include the post-NSS period, ensuring it remains a useful resource for policymakers, officials, practitioners, academics, and other relevant stakeholders. Compiled by academics at King’s College London and partners from the UK’s Nuclear Security Capacity Building Programme (NSCBP), the NSBB provides a comprehensive and objective overview of the international nuclear security framework and its evolution. The authors are grateful for the continuing support of the Department of Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) which has enabled the book’s publication and updating, with the NSBB freely available in digital form. The NSBB offers contextual information on nuclear and radioactive materials to explain the nature of the threat, and examines international agreements and guidance considered by the authors to be most relevant to nuclear security. The NSBB also serves as a comprehensive reference manual by consolidating the texts of key international instruments, conventions, and informal initiatives. The latest version of the NSBB builds on previous iterations, while also reflecting on latest developments in the field. This includes the aftermath of the NSS process and recent international convening events for nuclear security, such as the Conference of the Parties to the Amendment to the Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material in 2022 and the International Conference on Nuclear Security (ICONS) in 2024. sentences: Până acum, și-au mai anunțat intenția de a candida Fiodor Gagauz, fost deputat în Parlament, Alexandr Stoianoglo, fost procuror general și actual deputat al fracțiunii „Alternativa”, precum și fostul deputat Petr Vlah.

Procuratura Generală, sesizată Mihaela Tobultoc • 17/11/2026 11:50 Siegfried Mureșan, după întâlnire cu Maia Sandu, la Bruxelles: UE trebuie să pregătească noi fonduri pentru Republica Moldova de la 1 ianuarie 2028 Mihaela Tobultoc • 17/11/2026 21:43 „Republica Moldova nu este singură.

Liderul organizației teritoriale a Partidului Socialiștilor a anunțat într-o conferință de presă că a luat această decizie întrucât nu cunoaște „limba moldovenească”, în contextul în care noile prevederi ale Codului Electoral, adoptate în august, obligă candidații să cunoască limbile română și găgăuză.

La o conferință de presă susținută alături de liderul partidului, Igor Dodon, parlamentarul a acuzat majoritatea parlamentară că a modificat intenționat, cu puțin timp înainte de alegeri, Codul electoral, introducând o normă care limitează participarea la scrutin a persoanelor care nu vorbesc limba de stat.
Am luat decizia de a nu-mi depune candidatura la alegerile pentru funcția de bașcan”, a declarat Uzun, care a criticat noile prevederi ale Codului Electoral.
Igor Dodon a mai declarat, că modificarea legislației electorale cu doar două săptămâni înainte de perioada electorală este contrară Constituției și practicilor europene.
Condiția privind cunoașterea limbii trebuia să fie introdusă începând cu următorul ciclu electoral, peste patru ani”, a afirmat Dodon.
Scrutinele se vor desfășura după noile prevederi ale Codului Electoral al Republicii Moldova, întrucât Codul Electoral al autonomiei nu mai este valabil.
În listele electorale din regiune sunt înscriși în jur de 129.000 de alegători.

sentences: Staffing of the Election Administration, including the Central Election Commission’s controversial head, have been front and centre of the dispute, with other issues including penalties for parties not taking up their seats in parliament also causing a continued rift between the government and opposition.
Among the main demands of the opposition is that Tamar Zhvania, the Chair of the Central Election Commission (CEC), resign.

Dispute over electoral reforms heats up as Georgian election looms Log In News Stories In Focus Opinion and Editorial Newsletters Culture Daily Brief Advertise with Us About Us Jobs Charles Michel Agreement Dispute over electoral reforms heats up as Georgian election looms by Shota Kincha • 5 min read Share ▲ Parliamentary elections 2020.
A dispute over electoral reforms is heating up in Georgia ahead of crucial local elections, the result of which will determine if snap parliamentary elections follow in 2022.
On 18 June, the Council of Europe’s Venice Commission and OSCE’s Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights (ODIHR) published a joint opinion on the election code amendment bill.

Transparent staffing of electoral commissions According to the revised draft amendment, the CEC, the top management body of the Electoral Administration, is to be composed of 17 members including the chair, instead of the current 12, and to include at least seven non-partisan members with a maximum of nine from political parties.
Electoral reforms were a part of an EU-brokered agreement in April to end the political impasse between the government and opposition parties.
As part of the agreement, Georgian Dream also committed to calling the early parliamentary elections if they won less than 43% of proportional votes.
While this was not explicitly mentioned in the April deal, several opposition groups have insisted this is a precondition to gain public trust in the upcoming local elections slated for October.
Following the parliamentary vote last autumn, Zhvania and the CEC were accused of electoral fraud, which was followed by all opposition groups boycotting the new parliament for months.
The OSCE/ODIHR observation mission did not question the legitimacy of the final electoral outcome.
Electoral changes are only a part of the dispute.

[Read more on OC Media : Amnesty controversy threatens to derail EU-brokered deal in Georgia ] ‘A demonstration of force’ To implement the electoral reforms promised in the agreement, Georgian Dream initially tabled a draft in March, and resubmitted it in May together with Citizens and European Socialists, opposition groups that took up their seats in parliament as early as January.

However, parliament’s electoral reform task force still lacks inclusivity as unlike smaller parties, the UNM-dominated bloc that garnered 36 seats in the 150-member parliament, have refused to sign the April deal, even after ending their parliamentary boycott in May.

While the April agreement effectively dismantled the already shaky opposition front that had earlier vowed to jointly force Georgian Dream to call the snap elections, most opposition groups remain critical of how the governing party plans to proceed with the reforms.

The Venice Commission and ODIHR underlined the need for more robust transparency in staffing non-partisan members, a call that reflected criticism by most watchdogs and opposition groups that in recent years have described the non-partisan members as frequently lobbying for or being biased in favour of the ruling party.

Photo: Mariam Nikuradze/OC Media Most electoral reform advocates support the idea of staffing the CEC with only non-partisan, ‘professional’ members in the future but also consider it unrealistic to do so immediately.

On 15 June, election watchdog group ISFED underlined that for the sake of transparency, the special selection committee should be obliged to justify their choices for ‘professional’ CEC membership candidacies.

In the recent elections, local observers have highlighted the problems caused by a heavy presence of party activists outside polling stations, something they argue increases the risks of voter control and intimidation.

For the upcoming election, the authorities are mulling introducing some electronic voting technologies, possibly including poll pads to check in voters, electronic voting machines, and facial recognition devices.
However, so far, Georgia lacks the legal framework to regulate the application of these technologies as well as enough time before the election to widely integrate them in the voting process.

He focuses on nationalism, far-right movements, gender, and queer issues, with an eye on Eastern and Central Europe.
Since the 2020 parliamentary elections, Georgia has experienced political deadlock.
Following weeks of internal debates and almost 14 months after 2020’s parliamentary elections, leading UNM member Khatia Dekanoidze announced the decision on Monday.

Comrat regional authorities formally acknowledged the vacancy on August 17. tool.excerpt: Electrical transformer explosion triggers deadly fire in Phuket, killing 11 - tl;dr daily news Briefing World U.S. Business Technology Entertainment Sports Search... ⌘K Search Login Home world Electrical transformer explosion triggers deadly fire in Phuket, killing 11 November 16, 2026 at 09:45 AM • 3 min read • Source: Al Jazeera Photo: Al Jazeera TL;DR A fire in a mixed-use building in Patong, Phuket, killed 11 people and injured others early Monday. Authorities attribute the blaze to an exploding electrical transformer, which ignited combustible materials in a ground-floor motorcycle shop. The incident highlights ongoing concerns regarding building safety in Thai tourist hubs, following a similar mass-casualty fire in Bangkok in July. Key points At least 11 people died and 16 to 30 others were injured in a fire at a building in Patong, Phuket, starting around 2:00-3:17 AM local time. The building housed a restaurant, rented accommodation, and a motorcycle rental shop on the ground floor, which stored approximately 100 motorcycles, gas, engine oil, and plastic materials. Police and officials ruled out arson, citing an exploding electrical transformer near the building as the likely cause, which ignited the combustible materials and produced thick, toxic smoke. Victims were found on the third, fourth, and fifth floors, indicating they attempted to escape upward due to smoke blocking lower exits; no tourists were among the dead or injured. This is the second major fire causing mass casualties in Thailand since July, when a Bangkok bar fire killed about 40 people due to an electrical short circuit. Background Thailand has faced scrutiny over health and safety regulations in commercial and entertainment venues. In 2012, a fire in a Phuket club killed four people, and in 2009, a Bangkok club fire during New Year celebrations killed 67. The July 2026 Bangkok bar fire, which killed approximately 40, intensified calls for stricter enforcement of safety standards in crowded public spaces. How outlets are covering it Al Jazeera and AP News report 16 and 17 injured, respectively, while Thai PBS World states over 30 were injured, primarily from smoke inhalation. All sources agree on the 11 fatalities and the transformer explosion as the cause. tool.excerpt: The CEC announces the Legal Periods for the 2026 Legislative Elections | PNN English Français العربية Our Services Contact us Quick tour Politics Prisoners Human Rights Culture Opinion Nonviolence PNN TV Reports International Economy News Ticker The CEC announces the Legal Periods for the 2026 Legislative Elections Posted On: 23-07-2026 | National News Bethlehem / PNN / The Central Elections Commission (CEC) announced today, Wednesday, the table of legal periods for the 2026 Legislative Elections, scheduled for November 28, 2026, in accordance with the Presidential Decree issued for this purpose, and in line with the provisions of the General Elections Law No. (1) of 2007, and its amendments. The CEC clarified that voter registration centers in the West Bank will open its doors Saturday morning, August 15, 2026, for a period of 5 days, to be closed on Wednesday evening, August 19, 2026. Concerning the nomination stage, submission of nomination applications will be open on Saturday morning, September 26, 2026, for a period of 12 days, and shall be closed on Wednesday evening, October 7, 2026. Meanwhile, electoral campaigning will be launched starting Friday, November 6, 2026, for a period of 21 days. Electoral campaigning activities shall be halted – electoral silence/blackout, on Friday, November 27, 2026. Early voting for members of security forces will be conducted on November 26, 2026, whereas polling day for the general public will be Saturday, November 28, 2026. Meanwhile, electoral campaigning will be launched starting Friday, November 6, 2026, for a period of 21 days. Electoral campaigning activities shall be halted – electoral silence/blackout, on Friday, November 27, 2026. Early voting for members of security forces will be conducted on November 26, 2026, whereas polling day for the general public will be Saturday, November 28, 2026.
